speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent, and I am here to evaluate the newborn presenting with yellowish discoloration of the skin. To begin our assessment, when did you first notice the jaundice, and was it present within the first 24 hours of life?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-day-old male newborn. The newborn's mother reports that her child has developed yellowish discoloration of the skin that started from the face and then spread to the trunk since the past day. There have been no changes in his bowel habits or urination. The baby was born full-term at 38 weeks’ gestation via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has been exclusively breastfed every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Doctor
text: The jaundice appearing after the first 24 hours in a well-fed, full-term infant is reassuring and suggests a benign cause rather than hemolysis. I need to assess his clinical status further, so please tell me: is the baby feeding well and gaining weight appropriately?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Yellowish discoloration of the skin. I also have Discoloration started from the face then spread to the trunk, Scleral icterus noted.

speaker: Doctor
text: The progression of jaundice from the face to the trunk and the presence of scleral icterus are consistent with rising bilirubin levels. I need to quantify this elevation, so REQUEST TEST: Total and direct serum bilirubin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The bilirubin levels are mildly elevated with a predominant unconjugated fraction, which is typical for this age. To distinguish between breast milk jaundice and breastfeeding jaundice, has the baby lost more than 10% of his birth weight, or is he having fewer than six wet diapers per day?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Born full term at 38 weeks via uncomplicated vaginal delivery. No past medical history. Social history: Exclusive breastfeeding every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Doctor
text: The infant is feeding well and appears clinically stable with mild unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, which is consistent with a benign etiology. Given the onset after the first week of life and exclusive breastfeeding, this presentation is classic for breast milk jaundice. DIAGNOSIS READY: Breast milk jaundice
